description:
The Keetpalan Kaksh scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2021. 

This initiative aims to provide support and assistance to farmers and agricultural workers. 

The scheme is particularly focused on enhancing the productivity of crops and ensuring food security. 

It is designed to address the challenges faced by farmers in terms of pest control and crop protection. 

The primary objective of the Keetpalan Kaksh scheme is to establish a network of pest control centers across rural areas. 

These centers are intended to provide farmers with access to modern pest management techniques and resources. 

The government has set a target to establish at least 5,000 pest control centers by the end of 2025. 

Each center is expected to serve approximately 1,000 farmers in its vicinity. 

The benefits of the Keetpalan Kaksh scheme include access to expert advice on pest management. 

Farmers will receive training on integrated pest management practices. 

The scheme also includes the distribution of pest control materials at subsidized rates. 

Farmers can avail of a subsidy of up to 50% on the purchase of pest control products. 

This subsidy is aimed at reducing the financial burden on farmers. 

The eligibility criteria for the Keetpalan Kaksh scheme include being a registered farmer. 

Farmers must possess a valid land ownership document. 

The scheme is open to farmers of all ages. 

However, priority is given to small and marginal farmers. 

Small farmers are defined as those owning less than 2 hectares of land. 

Marginal farmers own less than 1 hectare of land. 

To apply for the Keetpalan Kaksh scheme, farmers must follow a specific process. 

The first step is to visit the nearest agricultural extension office. 

Farmers need to fill out an application form available at these offices. 

Required documents include proof of land ownership and identity verification. 

Farmers must also provide details about their farming practices and the crops they cultivate. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by agricultural officers. 

The review process typically takes about 15 days. 

If approved, farmers will receive a notification regarding their eligibility. 

The disbursement of benefits under the scheme occurs on a quarterly basis. 

Farmers can expect to receive subsidies directly into their bank accounts. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 500 crores for the implementation of this scheme. 

This budget is expected to cover the establishment of pest control centers and the distribution of subsidies. 

The implementing authority for the Keetpalan Kaksh scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The ministry has set up a dedicated helpline for farmers to seek assistance. 

Farmers can contact the helpline at 1800-180-1551 for queries related to the scheme. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to promote sustainable agriculture practices in India. 

By providing farmers with the necessary tools and knowledge, the government aims to increase crop yields. 

This is crucial for ensuring food security in a country with a population exceeding 1.4 billion. 

The Keetpalan Kaksh scheme also emphasizes the importance of eco-friendly pest management. 

Farmers will be encouraged to adopt organic pest control methods. 

This aligns with the government's vision of promoting organic farming in India. 

The scheme is expected to benefit over 5 million farmers across the country. 

This will significantly contribute to improving the livelihoods of rural households. 

The government is also collaborating with agricultural universities for research and development. 

These collaborations aim to innovate pest management techniques suitable for Indian conditions. 

The Keetpalan Kaksh scheme is aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations. 

Particularly, it focuses on Goal 2 which aims to end hunger and promote sustainable agriculture. 

The scheme will also monitor the impact of pest management on crop yields. 

Regular assessments will be conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the pest control measures. 

Farmers will be encouraged to provide feedback on the services received. 

This feedback will be crucial for making necessary adjustments to the scheme. 

The government plans to publish annual reports detailing the progress of the Keetpalan Kaksh scheme. 

These reports will include statistics on the number of farmers served and the increase in crop yields. 

The Keetpalan Kaksh scheme represents a significant step towards empowering farmers. 

By providing them with the necessary resources and knowledge, the government aims to foster a more resilient agricultural sector. 

The scheme is expected to create a ripple effect in rural economies. 

Increased agricultural productivity will lead to higher incomes for farmers. 

This, in turn, will stimulate local markets and create job opportunities. 

Overall, the Keetpalan Kaksh scheme is a comprehensive initiative. 

It addresses multiple aspects of agricultural sustainability and farmer welfare. 

The government's commitment to this scheme reflects its dedication to improving the agricultural landscape in India. 

Farmers are encouraged to take advantage of this scheme for better pest management. 

By doing so, they can enhance their productivity and ensure a sustainable future for their farms.
